artists.biography:
The Charlatans (known in the United States as The Charlatans UK) are an English alternative rock band. The band's line-up currently comprises Tim Burgess (vocals), Mark Collins (guitar), Martin Blunt (bass), Tony Rogers (keyboards) and Jon Brookes (drums and percussion).
 
Former members of the band include guitarist Jon Day (Jonathan Baker) (1989-1991), vocalist Baz Ketley (1989) and keyboardist Rob Collins (1989-1996), who died in a car accident during recording of their fifth album.
 
In the UK, all of the band's eleven studio albums have charted in the Top 40 in the UK Albums Chart, three of them being number ones. They have also achieved seventeen Top 30 singles, and four Top 10 hits in the UK Singles Chart.

perplexity.description:
Between 10th and 11th, released in 1992 by British rock band The Charlatans, is the group's second studio album and a defining work in their early discography. Following the success of their debut Some Friendly, the album marked a shift in the band's sound, blending their signature Madchester and baggy influences with a more polished, dance-oriented approach. Produced by Flood, the record features crisp, layered production that highlights the band's knack for hypnotic rhythms, swirling organ lines, and catchy hooks. Standout tracks like "Weirdo," "Tremolo Song," and "I Don’t Want To See The Sights" showcase the group's ability to merge 1960s and 1970s rock references with unrelenting dance beats, resulting in a sound that was both retro and modern for its time.

Commercially, Between 10th and 11th was a success, with "Weirdo" becoming the band's biggest US single and a UK Top 20 hit, while "Tremolo Song" and "I Don’t Want To See The Sights" also charted. The album solidified The Charlatans' reputation as one of the leading acts of the post-Madchester era, bridging the gap between indie rock and dance music. Critics praised its energy and consistency, with outlets like Entertainment Weekly and PopMatters hailing it as a classic of the genre. The album's enduring legacy is further cemented by its frequent inclusion in retrospectives of 1990s British rock.
